title: SS27 Men's Couture Craft and Techniques
summary: Hand craft in menswear: days of handwork on crystal denim, resin-dyed knits, hand-illustrated motifs and tailoring cut for both men and women.

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body:
- Philipp Plein's crystal-encrusted denim takes days of handwork<sup>[1]</sup>.
- Brunello Cucinelli dyed cable knits with resin so each sun-faded piece is unique<sup>[2]</sup>.
- Yohji Yamamoto showed a hand-illustrated bird tee<sup>[3]</sup>; Sacai wove a vintage photo into a two-piece suit<sup>[3]</sup>.
- Martin Quad debuted in Milan with unusual tailoring techniques<sup>[1]</sup>.
- At couture, Elie Saab cut tuxedos and capes for both men and women and is expanding its menswear line<sup>[4]</sup>.

sections.heading: Translating to ready-to-wear
sections.body:
- One hand technique per piece (a hand-painted motif, a crystal seam line).
- Garment-dyed or resin-dyed knits for one-of-a-kind colour.
- Woven or engineered photographic prints for statement suits.

design_implications: - Budget hand labour into hero pieces only.
commercial_implications: - Tell the craft story on the label; price as limited.
